findings.claim: The audience paragraph added by MIN-SAFE-002 cross-references §12.1 ('Extract, do not reinvent') rather than §12.7.1 ('Minimal caller wrapper'). The sentence reads: '…your pre-push verification is covered by the SCP reusable workflow you wired in §12.1.' An adopter following the link would land in an architecture-philosophy section that does not describe the reusable workflow at all; §12.7.1 is the correct target.
findings.evidence: docs/adoption/ADOPT-001-project-onboarding.md line 1014: '**Adopter repos do not need this wrapper** — your pre-push verification is covered by the SCP reusable workflow you wired in §12.1, and the SHA-pinning warnings in the parent §12.7.9 do not apply to invocations from inside the SCP repo itself.' §12.1 (line 722-728) is titled 'Extract, do not reinvent' — a design-philosophy principle. §12.7.1 (line 759-805) is titled 'Minimal caller wrapper' and contains the `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` template that adopters 'wire in'. No safety or enforcement implication: the audience paragraph correctly excludes adopter repos regardless of which section is cited.
findings.impact: An adopter who reads the audience paragraph and follows '§12.1' finds architecture philosophy, not the caller-wrapper template. No security bypass; the wrapper exclusion is clear from the surrounding text ('Adopter repos do not need this wrapper'). Purely a usability and documentation accuracy gap.
findings.mitigation: Change '§12.1' to '§12.7.1' in the audience paragraph. One-character edit. Recommend folding into TF-020P-005b (audience-placement reorganisation — next ADOPT-001 structural pass) rather than a standalone fix-round, since the paragraph already correctly scopes the audience and no developer could misread the wrapper exclusion from the wrong cross-reference alone.

self_reported_concerns: MIN-SAFE-001 closure verification: line 111 of scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh was read at HEAD (commit b755cea) and the full warning text confirmed character-for-character against the R1 proposed replacement. The phrase 'wrapper results may not match CI' conveys that divergence is a consequential outcome, not a remote possibility — this closes the R1 finding's concern about 'may diverge' understating rejection probability.

MIN-SAFE-002 closure verification: all four R1 criteria satisfied — (a) audience paragraph is the first paragraph of §12.7.9.1, appearing before any wrapper invocation guidance; (b) '**Audience: SCP-repo rule authors only.**' is in Markdown bold; (c) 'Adopter repos do not need this wrapper' is present verbatim; (d) 'the SHA-pinning warnings in the parent §12.7.9 do not apply to invocations from inside the SCP repo itself' is an explicit disclaimer of the parent section's SHA-clone-checkout requirement.

Advisory-only bypass concern (R2 check item 4): the 'treat wrapper output as advisory only' clause is syntactically parallel to 'install the pinned version' — both are operator responses to a version-mismatch warning. The clause is not a global permission to ignore CI; it says the wrapper's own output (under version drift) is advisory, which is the documented design. CI's enforcement is independent of whether the operator heeds the wrapper. No bypass surface created.

Symmetric awk parsers (COR-nit-001): the gsub(/[[:space:]]/, '', $2) operation operates entirely within awk; the captured version string is passed to a shell variable and used only in two contexts — string comparison ([[ '${pinned}' != '${installed}' ]]) and interpolation into the warning message (emit_warn). Neither context evaluates the string as a command. A crafted 'opa version' output containing shell metacharacters cannot escape into shell execution through this path.

Threshold-90 literal confirmation: scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh line 219 reads '--threshold 90' as a literal argument to opa test. No variable expansion, no env-var override path. Confirmed unchanged by fix-round-1 deltas.

CODEOWNERS coverage: CODEOWNERS line 55 carries 'scripts/** @jrnb2024'. scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh is covered. No change from R1 baseline. In single-operator count=0 mode this is documentary; in multi-maintainer mode it is machine-enforced per ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 and the ORDERING INVARIANT comment in CODEOWNERS.
summary: R2 SAFETY/BYPASS — TF-020P-005 fix-round-1 verified clean. MIN-SAFE-001 closed: scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh line 111 reads exactly 'local ${installed} differs from CI-pinned ${pinned} (scripts/.tool-versions) — wrapper results may not match CI; install the pinned version or treat wrapper output as advisory only' — exact proposed text, communicates non-trivial divergence likelihood. MIN-SAFE-002 closed: ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 first paragraph is '**Audience: SCP-repo rule authors only.**' in bold, states 'Adopter repos do not need this wrapper', explicitly disclaims '…the SHA-pinning warnings in the parent §12.7.9 do not apply to invocations from inside the SCP repo itself' — all four R1 verification criteria met. Audience paragraph does not say or imply 'CI is no longer the authoritative gate'; the §12.7.9.1 body closes with 'CI is still the authoritative gate — the wrapper is a CI-roundtrip saver, not a federation-conformance gate'. The 'advisory only' phrase in the version-drift warning is correctly scoped to wrapper output under version-mismatch conditions; it does not create a bypass surface (wrapper is informational by design; CI enforcement is independent). COR-nit-001 symmetric awk parsers: pure parsing-robustness change, no shell-injection vector, no safety surface. COMP-MIN-002 comment update (§12.7.9 → §12.7.9.1): zero runtime impact. COR-nit-002 printf '' removal: zero runtime/safety impact. Full bypass-surface re-inventory (tampered binary / tampered wrapper / shadow PATH / shell injection / threshold drop / repo-root escape / concurrency / info disclosure) shows no regression across any dimension vs R1 baseline. FIX-ROUND-1.md disposition is internally consistent: all 5 described inline fixes match actual file state; COMP-MAJ-001 'no-action' rationale (executable bit verified via git ls-files --stage) is recorded and correct. One NIT finding filed (R2-SAFE-NIT-001): the audience paragraph cross-references §12.1 ('Extract, do not reinvent' — an architecture-philosophy section) rather than the correct §12.7.1 ('Minimal caller wrapper' — where the reusable workflow is wired). No safety implication; propose as TF-020P-005b extension.
